**This repo is Django itself, not your site.** `slugify` is in `django/utils/text.py:481`, and its logic matches upstream Django. I couldn't run the test suite because the `asgiref` dependency isn't installed. So I copied the function's logic into a script, ran it, and got this:

| Input | Default | `allow_unicode=True` |
|---|---|---|
| `Hello World` | `hello-world` | `hello-world` |
| `Ünïcödé café` | `unicode-cafe` | `ünïcödé-café` |
| `Straße` | `strae` ⚠️ | `straße` |
| `Ørsted Łódź` | `rsted-odz` ⚠️ | `ørsted-łódź` |
| `日本語` | `''` (empty!) ⚠️ | `日本語` |
| `C++ & C#` | `c-c` | `c-c` |
| `a/b.c` | `abc` | `abc` |

The ⚠️ rows are the usual cause of "mangled" slugs. Without `allow_unicode=True`, `slugify` turns accents into ASCII and silently drops any character that has no ASCII form. So `ß`, `Ø` and `Ł` disappear, and non-Latin titles come out empty, which can also make different titles produce the same slug.

**Why I didn't just edit it:** this function is used by every project that runs this Django code. Changing it would change slugs for existing records and could break URLs that are already live. The fix most likely belongs in your app's code, not here.

Can you send one or two real titles and the URLs they turned into? Also, are you calling `slugify(...)`, the `|slugify` template filter, or a `SlugField` in the admin? Depending on the answer, the fix is one of these:
- Use `slugify(title, allow_unicode=True)` with `SlugField(allow_unicode=True)` if you're fine with Unicode in URLs.
- Use a transliteration library (e.g. `unidecode`) before slugifying, so `ß` becomes `ss`, `Ø` becomes `O` and `日本語` becomes `ri-ben-yu`.
- Add a fallback for empty slugs, such as using the object's ID.

3. **Your site's code**, if you can share it. This folder is the Django framework source, not your project. The real fix (a transliteration step, `allow_unicode=True`, or a fallback when the slug comes out empty) most likely goes in your model or view.

It also never returns an empty slug, and `max_length` cuts long titles at a word boundary. With `pip install unidecode`, `日本語` becomes `ri-ben-yu` instead of falling back to the ID.

To use it, copy the file into your app and replace your calls:
```python
from .safe_slugify import safe_slugify
self.slug = safe_slugify(self.title, max_length=50, fallback=self.pk or "item")
```

Two caveats:
- **Existing URLs:** pages already on the site keep their old slugs. If you regenerate them, the old links will break unless you redirect old slugs to new ones.
- **Admin-generated slugs:** if your slugs are typed into the admin, the browser fills them in with its own JavaScript, so this function won't change those.
